## Purpose

This procedure describes the safe setup, operation, and maintenance of
the Thermo Scientific Sorvall ST8R centrifuge. The centrifuge is used
to separate substance mixtures of different densities and is integral
to sample preparation workflows across multiple laboratory SOPs.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Thermo Scientific Sorvall ST8/8R centrifuge in the
  EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Clinical centrifuges (see *SOP-L25*),
  microcentrifuges (see *SOP-L26*), or field-portable centrifuges
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, Pomona College

## Definitions

- **Balancing:** The process of pairing tubes of equal mass (within
  0.1 g) in opposite rotor positions; required to prevent rotor
  imbalance, vibration, and bearing damage.
- **Fixed-angle rotor:** A rotor that holds tubes at a fixed angle
  (typically 20--45° from vertical); particles pellet against the side
  and bottom of the tube.
- **g-force (relative centrifugal force, RCF):** The centrifugal
  acceleration expressed as a multiple of gravitational acceleration
  (9.81 m s^-2^); calculated as $RCF = 1.118 \times 10^{-5} \times r
  \times N^2$ where $r$ is the rotor radius in cm and $N$ is speed in
  rpm.
- **Pellet:** The solid material sedimented to the bottom (or side-
  bottom) of a centrifuge tube after centrifugation.
- **Supernatant:** The liquid layer remaining above the pellet after
  centrifugation; the fraction of interest in many extraction
  procedures.
- **Swinging-bucket rotor:** A rotor whose buckets pivot to a
  horizontal position during spinning; particles pellet at the base of
  the tube, producing a well-defined pellet and cleaner supernatant.

| Role              | Responsibility                              |

| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |

| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |

## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Rotating rotor stores significant kinetic energy; rotor
  or bucket failure can eject debris. Maintain a 30 cm clear zone
  around the centrifuge during operation. Never open the door until the
  rotor has come to a complete stop and the display confirms it.
- **Chemical:** Corrosive samples (salt solutions, acids, bases) can
  damage rotors and accessories if not cleaned promptly after use.
- **Biological:** Pathogenic or biohazardous samples require sealed
  tubes or biosafety rotor lids. The centrifuge is not aerosol-tight in
  the event of mechanical failure.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling samples)

### Emergency Procedures

In the event of a hazardous spill or rotor failure:

1. Turn off the power supply immediately; pull the power plug if
   necessary
2. Leave the area and do not attempt to open the centrifuge
3. Contact the lab manager and refer to
   [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
4. The emergency door release may be used only to recover samples
   during a power failure, not during mechanical failure

## Procedure

### Site Selection and Setup

1. Operate the centrifuge indoors only
2. Place on a horizontally leveled, rigid surface with adequate
   load-bearing capacity
3. Maintain a safety zone of at least 30 cm around the centrifuge; do
   not place any hazardous substances within this zone
4. Ensure the setup location is well-ventilated and not exposed to heat
   or direct sunlight
5. Plug the centrifuge only into properly grounded sockets
6. Keep the main plug freely accessible at all times

### Preparation

1. Inspect the rotor, buckets, and accessories for signs of corrosion,
   cracks, or removed protective coating; do not use damaged components
2. Do not modify the mechanical components of the rotor or alter any
   electronic components of the centrifuge
3. Load the rotor properly: always balance samples symmetrically
4. Never overload the rotor beyond its rated capacity
5. Verify that the rotor is locked securely into place before closing
   the door
6. When working with corrosive samples, ensure tubes are fully sealed

::: {.callout-important}
### Hazardous Substances

- Do not centrifuge explosive or flammable materials
- Do not centrifuge toxic, radioactive, or pathogenic materials without
  appropriate safety precautions and sealed rotor lids
- The centrifuge is neither inert nor explosion-protected; never
  operate in an explosion-prone environment
- Use fully sealed tubes for highly corrosive substances that could
  impair rotor mechanical stability
:::

### Operation

1. Close the centrifuge door before starting a run
2. Set the desired speed, temperature (8R model), and time using the
   control panel
3. Press START to begin the run
4. Do not move, lean on, or place anything on top of the centrifuge
   while it is running
5. Implement measures to ensure that personnel do not remain near the
   centrifuge longer than necessary during operation
6. Wait until the rotor has come to a complete stop and the display
   confirms it before opening the door
7. Never open the centrifuge while the rotor is spinning

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Press the STOP key to shut down the centrifuge at any time. In an
emergency, pull the power supply plug to disconnect power immediately.
:::

### Shutdown and Cleanup

1. Remove samples promptly after the run is complete
2. Inspect the rotor and chamber for spills or condensation
3. If corrosive samples were centrifuged, clean the rotor, buckets, and
   chamber thoroughly with deionized water and dry before storage
4. If toxins or pathogenic substances have contaminated the centrifuge,
   carry out appropriate disinfection before further use
5. Wipe down the exterior of the centrifuge
6. Leave the door slightly ajar to allow the chamber to dry (if no
   hazardous residues are present)

### Cover Panel and Door Safety

1. Never operate the centrifuge if cover panels are damaged or missing
2. Do not attempt to bypass the door interlock mechanism
3. If mechanical failure occurs (rotor or bucket crash), the centrifuge
   is not aerosol-tight; leave the room and contact the lab manager


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Visually inspect the rotor and accessories before each use for
  cracks, corrosion, or wear
- Verify that samples are properly balanced before every run
- Confirm the door closes and latches securely
- Report any unusual vibrations, noises, or error messages to the lab
  manager immediately
- Follow the manufacturer's maintenance schedule in the instruction
  manual


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Contaminated cleaning materials | Dispose per [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) if hazardous chemicals were involved |
| Damaged rotors or accessories | Contact lab manager for proper disposal  |
| Biohazardous spill materials  | Autoclave before disposal                |

## Training Record

Before operating the Sorvall ST8R centrifuge independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the manufacturer's instruction manual
4. Observe a trained operator perform rotor loading, a centrifuge run,
   and post-run cleanup
5. Demonstrate proper sample balancing, rotor installation, and
   emergency shutdown under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
